title: ideas for unload/reduce context
author: Solid-Funny-668
selftext:
The whole thing is perfectly working on claude and chatgpt but those are web based chats. Once i shift it to a local Ai like LM Studio it cant event run. I try both qwen2.5-32b and magnum-22B but both can even read the files correctly.

any one had similar situation that have any suggestions?

https://github.com/west132/AI-GM-Engine.git

comments.author: skill-tap
comments.body:
Your co-dev agent may be surprisingly resourceful for finding the solution, they'll know the inner working better than most.

I'd update the git to reflect "works with these models" followed by something like "local model support pending".

It wasn't clear from GitHub, is the game running via the LLM, or does the agent simply interface with the game? Is the context window bloated at load, or is good at first and grows too quick?

replies.author: Solid-Funny-668
replies.body:
i basically only run at LLM. but claude’s basic plan burn usage too fast so i was planning to try on lm studio with local ai(3090ti). but it cant even load the files to start round 1. 
maybe when claude usage back i could as it, cause i am really new on lm studio or any local ais

replies.author: skill-tap
replies.body: To clarify the question, can the game be ran on it's own?

replies.author: skill-tap
replies.body:
From what I think I know, the game should probably run on it's own without the LLM. Code executes real-time, like when your character faces an obstacle and you press space to jump, there no room for the latency an LLM brings to the mix. Ask your co-dev for some guidance on running the game locally without agent integration, then layer in the agent integration. 

I'm not saying the other approach is wrong, or can't work. Brave new world, new tech, new approaches, don't let others limit your creative process. It's just a nod towards what should work.

comments.author: Dry_Map_4545
comments.body: maybe develop it on your own
